external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: Engineer who uses the dispatch console from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The method by which an engineer signs in is not recorded.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: Single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers and connected to the dispatch API, including a WebSocket for live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: The console and API are served from different origins. CORS configuration is not recorded. WebSocket TLS, handshake authentication, and post-connection session checking are not recorded.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: Host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: API in the production control plane called by the console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.notes: The API is not reachable from the internet. CORS allowed origins and credential handling are not recorded.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: Hourly importer that retrieves and parses the scheduling partner's XML work schedule, archives the downloaded document, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: Database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: The database's protection at rest is not recorded. Job orders carry the token or session that created them, but nothing about the person behind that token.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: Folder on the corporate file store containing each downloaded scheduling document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: load application
data_flows.description: Duty engineer loads the dispatch console application from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: Duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: The engineer sign-in method is not recorded.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: Dispatch console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin; CORS origins and credential handling are not recorded.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: Dispatch console opens and maintains a WebSocket to receive live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Whether the socket uses TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, and whether the engineer's session is checked again after connection are not recorded.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: Dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull feed
data_flows.description: Schedule importer pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS every hour.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: How the partner identifies the importer and how the importer identifies the partner are not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.description: Schedule importer writes each downloaded scheduling document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: Schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Corporate network where duty engineers and the schedule importer are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: Company-controlled zone holding the live estate, where an account can move a crew or change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: Trust zone controlled by the scheduling partner, another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch console runs on the duty engineer's browser within the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The duty engineers are stated to sit on the corporate network and use the browser-based console.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch console is internally exposed rather than internet-facing.
assumptions.basis: It is used by duty engineers on the corporate network, and no internet exposure is stated.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate web host presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The text identifies it as a web host that serves a browser application.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is a cross-origin API called by a browser console and also exposes a WebSocket.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule importer presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a scheduled batch importer that pulls, parses, archives, and posts work orders.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: It holds crew names, mobile numbers, credentials or sessions, and operational job orders.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule archive's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: It holds commercially sensitive planned work documents.
